newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK blue chips seen soft, red chips to move ahead.
newsitem.headline: HK blue chips seen soft, red chips to move ahead.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are set for a mixed session on Thursday, with blue chips likely to feel more downward pressure from concerns about the government's future housing policy while red chips push ahead, brokers said.
"It has become a two-tier market," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.
"The general market probably will be down but the red chips will stand out with a lot of news happening."
Weakness on Wall Street and in London overnight was likely to dampen market sentiment, already hurt by speculation about government plans to cool down rising property prices, Mak said.
The Hang Seng Index fell 103.26 points to 14,203.89 on Wednesday. Later, the Hang Seng London Reference Index slipped a further 38.03 points, or 0.27 percent, to 14,165.86.
"I think the market will move sideways," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities. "People are not interested in buying property stocks."

But China Resources' purchase of a stake in The Hongkong Chinese Bank, following China Everbright-IHD's deal to buy part of Everbright Bank of China, should continue to fuel speculation about asset injections in the red chip sector, push those stocks higher.
